The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T02:20:18Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-11T02:20:43Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
Broken from 2026-11-11T02:14:00Z {began} (the onset, dated to its minute: a change came during that minute) to 2026-11-11T02:22:00Z {back_to_normal}, when the metrics show it back to normal.
That is 8 minutes {duration}, and every impact figure below is measured over that stretch.
Argus held the incident for 2 minutes 27 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-11T02:23:06Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 1.0% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 26.3% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 38.5% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 25.3% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 0.9916666666666666% {series_before} before it began, 26.3125% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 38.5% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: 5,182.30 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-11T02:20:39Z {T1.1} Argus: Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-11T02:20:44Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-11T02:20:44Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-11T02:20:50Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 02:20:18 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-11T02:20:54Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 360 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-11T02:20:55Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 02:14 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-11T02:20:55Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-11T02:20:57Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 {T8.2} day 1 {T8.3} minute before Nov 11 02:15 {T8.4}
  - [T9] 2026-11-11T02:20:57Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 1 {T9.2} production change
  - [T10] 2026-11-11T02:20:58Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 8 {T10.2} minutes before 02:20 {T10.3}
  - [T11] 2026-11-11T02:20:58Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 35 {T11.2} log lines
  - [T12] 2026-11-11T02:20:58Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 {T12.2} replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
  - [T13] 2026-11-11T02:20:59Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 1 {T13.2} candidate cause, best first: C1
  - [T14] 2026-11-11T02:20:59Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T15] 2026-11-11T02:20:59Z {T15.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 2 {T15.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T15.3} hour before 02:20:59 {T15.4}
  - [T16] 2026-11-11T02:21:03Z {T16.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T17] 2026-11-11T02:21:04Z {T17.1} Argus: Called in the Mitigation Agent
  - [T18] 2026-11-11T02:21:09Z {T18.1} Mitigation Agent: Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF
  - [T19] 2026-11-11T02:21:17Z {T19.1} Mitigation Agent: Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 02:22 {T19.2} - up to 170s {T19.3}
  - [T20] 2026-11-11T02:23:06Z {T20.1} Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 02:21 {T20.2}
  - [T21] 2026-11-11T02:23:06Z {T21.1} Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
  - [T22] 2026-11-11T02:23:06Z {T22.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - set flag [monthly-spend-feature] OFF and the rule that fired stopped firing
  - [T23] 2026-11-11T02:24:45Z {T23.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/530

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-11T02:14:28Z {P1.1} flag-toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
  - [P2] 2026-11-11T02:20:18Z {P2.1} flag-toggle an-unrelated-feature by admin: feature flag an-unrelated-feature was switched on - found only by Argus's read of the flag provider's history: it came after 2026-11-11T02:15:00Z {P2.2}, where the investigation's reads of the changes ended
  - Deploys read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G7e5d] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 {G7e5d.1} evaluations - 2 {G7e5d.2} occurrences in 2 {G7e5d.3} minutes, 02:12–02:13 {G7e5d.4}
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 3 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 2 {G46bc.2} minutes, 02:12–02:13 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 9 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 9 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 02:12–02:20 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 38.50% {Gbac1.5}, typically 28.00% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 02:15 {Gbac1.7}
  - [G971b] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 98 {G971b.1} / on 102 {G971b.2} - 200 {G971b.3} evaluations - 1 {G971b.4} occurrence in 1 {G971b.5} minute, 02:14 {G971b.6}
  - [G5309] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 {G5309.1} occurrences in 7 {G5309.2} minutes, 02:14–02:20 {G5309.3}
  - [Gce95] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 {Gce95.1} evaluations - 6 {Gce95.2} occurrences in 6 {Gce95.3} minutes, 02:15–02:20 {Gce95.4}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1] The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 2026-11-11T02:14:28Z {C1.1}. That enabled a code path that raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate stepped from about 1% {C1.2} to about 30% {C1.3}. No deployment was involved. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.95 {C1.4}, confirmed]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for [C1] (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault: `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py divides `account.total_this_month_cents` by `len(bought_this_month)`, the number of purchases flagged `in_current_month`. Most shoppers have bought before but not this month. For them that list is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError. That is the line the incident log names (spend_summary.py:47). Turning on monthly-spend-feature sent the account page's figure through this function, and every request for such a shopper failed.
      
      The flag was what triggered the incident, but the fault is in the code: the function has no answer for the normal case of a shopper who has bought nothing this month. With the fix, when there are no purchases this month the function returns 0 {F1.1}, because a shopper with no purchases this month has spent nothing this month. Otherwise it divides as before. Shoppers who did buy this month get the same result as before.
      
      Other code is unchanged. With the flag off, `render_spend_summary` still uses `average_spend_per_item`, and that function still raises for an account with no purchases at all. tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py and tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py expect that error, and that error is the only case the line-number test in test_account_page.py checks. Nothing in this change catches errors.
      
      The tests: the new cases in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py call `average_spend_per_item_this_month` and `render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True)` for a shopper whose purchases all fall outside the current month, and assert 0 {F1.2}. Against the current code both would raise ZeroDivisionError.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, done): Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature
  - AI-2 (prevent, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #530 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.
The document already states what set it off, in a section of its own: the change [P1].

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend figure goes through average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's total by the number of purchases made this month and has no case for a shopper who bought nothing this month. For such a shopper the number is zero, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and the page request fails. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: Turning on a feature switch made shoppers' account pages work out their average spend per item this month, and that sum fails by dividing by zero, likely for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.
still_at_risk: If monthly-spend-feature is switched on again before a fix is in place, account pages could fail again, likely for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.
symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account page requests failed with errors, and the account page error rate stayed high minute after minute. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3: At {P1.1} the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on. Before that, its evaluations came back all off. In the minute it was switched they were split, and after that they were all on. The division-by-zero errors began in the minute the flag was switched. (cites P1, under "Changes to production it read"; G7e5d, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G971b, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gce95, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 1: The switch-on of the flag an-unrelated-feature at {P2.1}. It came after the onset at {T6.2}, by which time the account page errors were already high. (cites P2, under "Changes to production it read"; T6, under "What Argus did, in order"; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 4: With the flag on, the account page divides the month's spend by the number of purchases made this month, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought nothing this month. (cites F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
contributing_factors 1: No check was seen before monthly-spend-feature was switched on in production that ran the flag-on code path for a shopper with no purchases this month.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been found before the flag reached shoppers, and the flag would not have been switched on.
contributing_factors 2: The flag went from off for all evaluations to on for all evaluations straight away. No staged rollout to a small share of shoppers, and nothing that stops a rollout on rising errors, was seen.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have hit the failing path, and the rollout could have been stopped before it reached everyone.
contributing_factors 3: An error while working out the spend summary failed the whole account page request rather than only leaving out that figure.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: Shoppers would still have got their account pages, just without the monthly spend figure, even with the division by zero still in place.
action_items 1: Require tests that run a feature flag's on path to pass before that flag can be switched on in production for io-shop.
action_items 2: Roll out feature flag changes on io-shop to a small share of traffic first, and stop the rollout automatically when the error rate rises.
action_items 3: Make the account page load without the spend summary when the summary fails, rather than failing the whole request.
action_items 4: Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page so that a person is paged when it fires.
action_items 5: Keep monthly-spend-feature off until a fix for the spend summary is merged and deployed.
went_wrong 1: Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was called to the incident.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
